headline.funnel_interpretation: The significant funnel plot asymmetry (egger's p=0.0276) indicates substantial publication bias in this meta-analysis on alcohol and prostate cancer. This specific pattern suggests that smaller studies with smaller or null effects may be underrepresented, compromising the reliability of the pooled estimate and potentially leading to an overestimation of the true association.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 26 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.27 (95% CI: 1.13–1.42), suggesting that alcohol is associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 86.04%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
